title: The Promise with a Time Attached

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked him. "There, in the tent," he said. Then one of them said, "I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance to the tent, which was behind him. - Gen 18:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The visitors ask for Sarah by name - a hint that these are no ordinary travellers. And then comes the promise, now with a specific timeline: "about this time next year... Sarah your wife will have a son." God had made this promise before, but now He fixes the date. The long-awaited miracle is one year away.

There is such kindness in God attaching a time to His promise. For decades Sarah had lived with vague future hope. Now God says, in effect, "The waiting is nearly over. This time next year." He knows how much we need not just promises but the assurance that they will come to pass, and soon.

Notice the detail: "Sarah was listening at the entrance to the tent." She overhears the promise, hidden behind the tent flap. God knew she was there. Nothing about this moment was accidental - God intended Sarah to hear, personally, the promise that would change her life.

God speaks to us where we are, even when we think we're just quietly listening on the edges. He had not forgotten Sarah in her decades of disappointment. The God who kept this appointment "when the set time had fully come" (Gal 4:4) keeps every appointment. Whatever promise you are waiting on, God has not forgotten. His timing, though slow to us, is exact.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you waiting on a promise, wondering if it will ever come?
- Can you trust that God's timing, though slow, is exact?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You attach Your perfect timing to Your promises and never forget. In my seasons of waiting, help me trust that You have not overlooked me. Your appointed time will surely come.
Amen.
